verses.1: After that, David asked the Lord, “I will go up to one of the cities of Judah.” The Lord said to him, “Go up.” David replied, “Yes, I will go.” Then the Lord said, “Your friend Nabal.”
verses.2: And David and his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, also went there. Abigail was the wife of Nabal from Carmel.
verses.3: And his men, whom David brought with him, settled in the towns of Hebron.
verses.4: And the people of Judah came and made David king over the house of Judah. They told David, “The people of Gibeah, who buried Shaul, have come.”
verses.5: David sent messengers to the people of Jabesh Gilead. He said to them, “You have done this kindness toward your gods and toward Shaul. Now, come here.” They obeyed him.
verses.6: And now, Jehovah will show you kindness and truth. And I too will do you good, just as you have done this.
verses.7: And now, strengthen your hands, and be like the children of life. For your leaders have died, and even I too will be destroyed in the house of Jehovah, by their king.
verses.8: And Abner, son of Ner, the commander of the army, who was taken away by Saul. Saul took Absalom and carried him away from his camp.
verses.9: And he ruled over the Hittites, the Assyrians, the Elamites, the Babylonians, the Medes, and all of Israel.
verses.10: At the age of forty, Shelemiah became king over Israel. He ruled for two years. But in the house of Judah, there were those who followed David as their king.
verses.11: And the number of days during which David was king over Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.12: And Abner, son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth, son of Saul, went out from their camps in Gibeon.
verses.13: And Joab, son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David went out. They met together at Gibeon. They sat down on one side of the altar, and they sat down on the other side of the altar.
verses.14: And Abner said to Joab, “Come forward, young men! Stand before us.” And Joab said, “I will come forward.”
verses.15: And they stood up and went through the number of twenty-two thousand men, along with Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twenty-two thousand servants of David.
verses.16: And they strengthened each other by supporting one another’s heads; they also destroyed their enemies from their side. They fell together, and they called out to that place, which was the territory of the Zulu people.
verses.17: The battle was extremely difficult on that day. Abner and the Israelites were defeated by David’s soldiers.
verses.18: And there were three sons of Seruya: Yoab, Abishai, and Asael. Asael was swift in his steps, just like one of those warriors who fought in the field.
verses.19: And Asheel followed Abner. But he didn’t go towards the right side, or towards Shemuel, after Abner.
verses.20: And Abner stood behind him, and he said, “You, this is Esaiel.” And Esaiel replied, “It’s me.”
verses.21: And Abner said to him, “Set your sword or your spear on your shoulder, and take one of the boys with you. Use his sword to protect yourself from your enemies.”
verses.22: And Abner said to Asahel, “Sit down by me. Why do I have to go away from you? How can I turn my face towards your brother Joab?”
verses.23: And he rushed towards the ship. Abner rushed after it, but the ship rushed away from him. It fell there, and Abner died under it. All those who came to that place also died.
verses.24: And Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. As the sun rose, they arrived at Gibeah of Amma, which is located on the road from the desert of Gibeon.
verses.25: And the sons of Benyamin gathered together after Abner. They became one group, and they stood on top of one hill.
verses.26: And Abner called for Joab and said, “Halanethzah will eat the flesh of Harel. You did not know that it would become a curse in the future. Until his death, he will never say to the people, ‘Return from behind their backs.’”
verses.27: And Joab said, “May God live! If only you hadn’t said that. Then, from morning onward, the people would have taken someone from among their own brothers.”
verses.28: And Joshua stood firm in his place. All the people stood there, without pursuing Israel any longer. They also stopped trying to fight against them.
verses.29: And Abner and his men walked around all that night. They crossed the Jordan River, and then they continued their journey along the entire length of Bethoron. Finally, they arrived at their campsites.
verses.30: And Joab returned from behind Abner’s tent. He gathered all the people together, and he appointed eleven or twelve men from David’s servants to be his commanders. And he did as he had planned.
verses.31: And the servants of David were killed in Benyamin and among the people of Abner: three thousand six hundred men died.
verses.32: And they carried Asherah away and buried her in the tomb of her father, who lived in Bethlehem. They spent the entire night there, with Yoab and his men, and they lit lamps for them in their company.
